name: dotclaude
description: A small Claude Code plugin with guards, model and effort rules, compaction and cache notes, and role agents.

guard_bash.title: Bash guard
guard_bash.description: Ask before destructive `git`, file system, and database commands, hook bypasses, and public side effects (a publish, `gh` writes, and Claude Design writes outside `/design-sync`). Deny recursive searches that walk gitignored build output.

guard_edit.title: Edit guard
guard_edit.description: Ask before edits that delete test assertions, add skip markers, touch generated files, or edit Claude settings files.

guard_secrets.title: Secret redaction
guard_secrets.description: Scan every tool output with Betterleaks and replace each secret it finds with `[REDACTED:<rule>]` before the model sees it. Needs `betterleaks` on `PATH`. Without it, output passes through and session start says so.

guard_agents.title: Subagent guard
guard_agents.description: Deny a subagent spawn that breaks the model and effort rules, with the reason.

codegraph.title: CodeGraph augment
codegraph.description: When a `Grep` call or a Bash `rg` or `grep` search looks for one symbol name in a project with a CodeGraph index, run `codegraph sync` if files changed since the last index, then add the callers and callees of that symbol to the search result. Adds nothing when the index has no function, method, or class with exactly that name. Rebuild an index in an old format with `codegraph index`. At session start in a git repository without an index, tell Claude to run `codegraph init`, which the Bash guard asks the user to approve. Needs `codegraph` on `PATH`.

ponytail.title: Minimal code rules
ponytail.description: At session start, tell Claude to build the minimum: no code that the task does not need, reuse before new code, and the standard library before a dependency. The idea comes from Ponytail.

compaction_handoff.title: Compaction handoff
compaction_handoff.description: Before an automatic compaction of the main conversation, fork a handoff note, then stop and tell the user to run `/clear` and continue from the note.

sembr.title: Semantic line breaks
sembr.description: Rewrap the prose of commit messages and `gh pr` or `gh issue` bodies with semantic line breaks before the command runs. After a `Write` or `Edit` of Markdown or code comments that break lines at a column, add the `sembr` text to the result. Needs `sembr` on `PATH`. Never rewrites a file.
